title: FAUST. XV. A disc wind mapped by CH<SUB>3</SUB>OH and SiO in the inner 300 au of the NGC 1333 IRAS 4A2 protostar
question: Explore the kinematics and chemical structure of the gas in the inner 300 au transition zone between the disk and outflowing material of the protostar NGC 1333 IRAS 4A2 using SiO and CH3OH.

data.sensitivity: σ_c = 8 x 10^-2 mJy beam^-1 (continuum); σ = 1 mJy beam^-1 per 1 km s^-1 channel (SiO), σ = 1.1 mJy beam^-1 per 1 km s^-1 channel (CH3OH)

evidence.quote: NGC 1333 IRAS 4A is a very well studied system in Perseus (∼300 pc away; Zucker et al. 2018).

evidence.loc: 3. The kinematical structure of the IRAS 4A inner regions
evidence.quote: (in the ranges (−6, −2) and (+2, +6) km s−1 with respect to the v sys ; v sys = 6.8 km s−1 ; Choi 2001)

what.value: H2 gas density of 2 x 10^6 cm^-3 in the inner 0''.24 of IRAS 4A2

evidence.loc: 3. The kinematical structure of the IRAS 4A inner regions
evidence.quote: Finally, in IRAS 4A2 De Simone et al. (2020) estimated an H 2 density of about 2 × 106 cm−3 in the inner 0′′. 24.

evidence.quote: Top: Spectral properties of CH 3 OH and SiO by Xu et al. (2008) and Müller et al. (2013), respectively, from the CDMS database (Müller et al. 2005).

evidence.quote: Regarding methanol, theoretical predictions by Ferrero et al. (2020) indicate a BE range of (3770–8618) K, while the pre-exponential factor ν des is 3.2 × 1017 s−1 (Minissale et al. 2022).

external_data.citation: Ferrero et al. (2020), Minissale et al. (2022)

evidence.quote: The binding energy of SiO is reported to be about 3500 K (Hasegawa & Herbst 1993), that translate into a sublimation temperature of about 50 K.

recipe.goal: Generate integrated intensity (moment 0) maps, channel maps, and PV diagrams to characterize kinematic structure
recipe.method: Integrate CH3OH and SiO emission over blue-shifted (-6 to -2 km s^-1 wrt v_sys) and red-shifted (+2 to +6 km s^-1 wrt v_sys) velocity ranges, bin channel maps to 1 km s^-1, and extract PV diagrams along 0''.1-wide slices parallel and perpendicular to the methanol/SiO PA.
key_parameters: Velocity ranges: (-6, -2) km s^-1 and (+2, +6) km s^-1 wrt v_sys = 6.8 km s^-1 (i.e., 0.8 to 4.8 km s^-1 and 8.8 to 12.8 km s^-1)
PV slice width = 0''.1, parallel slice length = 3''.6 (at PA ~ 30 deg), 7 perpendicular slices of length 1''.6 separated by 0''.3, plus ~7'' path following SiO structure

recipe.goal: Extract spectra at emission peaks and derive column densities and abundances
recipe.method: Identify pixels with the highest flux level in the (-6, -2) and (+2, +6) km s^-1 integrated maps for CH3OH and SiO, extract spectra at those peak positions, integrate line intensity in the blue and red velocity ranges, and compute column densities and abundance ratios assuming LTE optically thin emission.
key_parameters: Peak offsets wrt phase center: CH3OH Red Peak (-1''.35, +1''), SiO Red Peak (-1''.27, +0''.93), CH3OH Blue Peak (-1''.41, +1''.13), SiO Blue Peak (-1''.44, +1''.19)
Integration ranges: blue (0.8 to 4.8 km s^-1) and red (8.8 to 12.8 km s^-1)
assumptions: LTE, optically thin emission, excitation temperature T_ex = 100 K
H2 density = 2 x 10^6 cm^-3 in the inner 0''.24 (from De Simone et al. 2020)

recipe.goal: Evaluate thermal sublimation vs. shock sputtering and constrain wind inclination
recipe.method: Calculate species sublimation temperatures from binding energies and half-life desorption timescale (Eq. C.1-C.3), compare with optically thin dust temperature profile (Eq. C.4), and constrain wind inclination angle from observed line-of-sight velocities and minimum shock velocities required for sputtering.
key_parameters: Minimum sputtering velocity = 10 km s^-1 (or 35 km s^-1)
assumptions: Warm-up timescale t_1/2 ~ 10^4 yr; optically thin dust; bolometric luminosity of IRAS 4A2 L_* = 4.5 L_sun (half of total 9 L_sun)

score_reason: The ALMA data are public (2018.1.01205.L), and the spectral integration windows, peak pixel coordinate offsets, and LTE assumptions (T_ex = 100 K, spectroscopic constants in Table 1) are explicitly tabulated, making the post-imaging analysis highly reproducible. However, low-level self-calibration and GILDAS imaging parameters are omitted.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA Large Program data with clearly defined velocity integration ranges (0.8-4.8 and 8.8-12.8 km s^-1), explicit extraction coordinates, and straightforward single-line LTE column density calculations leading to numeric answer keys in Table 1.
